Subject: Planned westus3 rolling driver upgrade — May 22 service window

Hello —

We are scheduling a planned rolling driver upgrade in the westus3 region to address recent node-level stability regressions we observed at high token throughput. The maintenance is targeted for: 

  - Window: Sat, May 22 2027 01:00 — 03:00 UTC (Fri, May 21 18:00 — 20:00 PDT)
  - Impact: Rolling restarts of host VMs across the westus3 serving pool. Each host restart typically takes 90–180s; requests will be automatically routed to healthy hosts where capacity is available.
  - Scope: Dedicated and Hosted nodes in westus3 (no control plane downtime expected).

Mitigations in place:
  - Continuous incremental rollout: we will only take a small % of hosts out of rotation at a time to keep capacity headroom.
  - KV/prefix cache preservation where supported; active sessions will be reestablished.
  - Auto-fallback: traffic will route to equivalent model variants in other regions if capacity is constrained.

Actions we need from you:
  1) Confirm if you have any blackout constraints during the window.
  2) If you operate long-running jobs (e.g., large-batch inference), please pause or move them outside the window where possible.

Attachments: westus3_driver_runbook_v1.4.pdf (runbook, steps + rollback criteria)

We will post live status updates to our status page and share a concise post-maintenance note with a link to the postmortem. If you'd like a private runway or to delay for an upcoming launch, reply and we can coordinate.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

  - Can you confirm whether KV cache warmup is preserved for our dedicated pools or will we see cache misses for the first 5–10 minutes after our traffic shifts back?
  - What are the rollback criteria if the driver causes an increase in 5xx errors beyond baseline?
  - We have a scheduled nightly ingestion on May 22 02:30 UTC — can you advise if that will be interrupted and whether you recommend rescheduling?

We need this information so we can decide whether to request a blackout window.

Subject: RE: Planned westus3 rolling driver upgrade — May 22 service window

Marissa / team — looping in SRE and runtime leads to answer Borealis' questions and confirm rollback/monitoring. Internal plan below: 

  - KV cache: for dedicated pools with pinned instances, we will attempt cache-preservation logic; however there will be a measurable window (typically 2–8 minutes) of increased cold misses while session rehydration completes. We'll add an explicit warmup step in the runbook for the affected queues.
  - Rollback criteria: automatic rollback will trigger if 5xx error rate exceeds baseline by +0.5% sustained for 5 minutes OR if average tail latency increases > 50% for a 10-minute window. If rollback occurs, we will notify customers and open a follow-up incident.
  - Ingestion at 02:30 UTC: recommended to reschedule to outside the window if possible. If Borealis cannot move it, we will coordinate a temporary capacity bump prior to the ingestion to reduce risk.

Attachments: post_maintenance_checklist.txt

Marcus / Jonas / Dylan — please confirm the warmup step and the expected cold-miss window in your environment so I can reply to Borealis with concrete numbers. Also confirm the customer credit approach (I suggested a 2-hour credit if they see an SLA-affecting incident).

Thanks,
Monica Patel

Subject: Maintenance complete — westus3 driver upgrade (post-maintenance summary)

Hi Alex / team —

The rolling driver upgrade in westus3 completed at 07:42 UTC on May 22. Summary and customer-facing notes: 

  - What we did: Applied driver v1.12.3 with staged restarts across the westus3 host pool. The rollout used our small-batch cadence (max 6% hosts out at any time).
  - Observed impact: Most traffic routed without interruption. We observed one host that returned to service ~8 minutes later than expected due to an underlying disk health check; traffic was routed to healthy hosts during that time. No sustained customer-facing 5xx spike was recorded. Borealis reported no measurable service disruption for production traffic.
  - Follow-ups: We published a short postmortem and the artifact bundle (logs, runbook exec notes) here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-maintenance-windows
  - Credit: As discussed, we will proactively apply a 2-hour service credit to accounts that request review; if you believe you were affected, reply to this thread and Monica will open the credit request.

If you'd like a short debrief with the SRE/runtime team, we can set up a 30-minute call this week. Thank you for coordinating — appreciate the flexibility.

Best,
